vague_accusation: Ask for the specific example and the criterion used.
Keep a note of what was said without filling in a missing accusation.
guilt_induction: Write down the requested work separately from the loyalty language.
Check your actual commitments before accepting another demand.
dismissal_warning: Check whether the warning is formal, what criteria apply and what response is requested.
Record the words you remember and consider qualified support about your options.
public_criticism: Separate the work issue from any personal remarks and who witnessed them.
Keep details that help you describe the impact on you.
colleague_gossip: Check work-related claims directly when safe.
You do not owe participation in a personal verdict about an absent colleague.
unattributed_consensus: Ask for a specific concern and its example.
Record the collective claim as a claim rather than supplying unnamed supporters.
circular_interrogation: Identify the question that remains open and what you have already answered.
A factual follow-up or a pause can help you avoid endless self-defense.
moving_goalposts: Compare the written versions and note what changed.
Check the extra work, time and resource impact before recommitting.
withheld_information: List the information or access you need.
Keep a record of when you requested it and what work depends on it.
meeting_loop: Identify the actual decision, its owner and what remains open.
Check whether another meeting serves a useful next step for you.
responsibility_diffusion: Ask who has responsibility and who has authority to decide.
Check what you are being asked to own before accepting an unnamed obligation.
micromanagement: Record the requested updates and how they affect time for your work.
Check whether clear review points would give you a workable boundary.
competing_priorities: List the competing demands and request a priority decision.
Keep the trade-off visible rather than absorbing it as personal overtime.
credit_dispute: Keep the drafts, messages or work records that show your contribution.
Ask for the record to reflect the specific work you can verify.
workload_overload: Compare the new demand with your available time and current commitments.
Ask what will be removed, delayed or resourced before making another promise.
surveillance_concern: Check the actual monitoring or reporting policy where it is safe to do so.
Separate what you observed from unknown collection details and consider qualified advice.
no_response: Keep the unanswered question, your follow-up and the work impact together.
Do not treat silence as approval or fill in a decision for someone else.
suspected_retaliation: Keep the sequence of events and the concrete changes you observed.
Check confidentiality before sharing a sensitive record or seeking qualified support.
after_meeting_replay: Keep one factual note and any necessary next step.
Repeating the memory is not required to make the event matter.
ordinary_disagreement: Check the work question, the stated criteria and how the interaction affects you.
You can hold your view or ask a question without excusing disrespect.
